name: Mahogany Brown
lede: Mahogany Brown is a very dark reddish brown named for polished mahogany wood, and it is also the paint standard RAL 8016.

sections.title: The color of a wood
sections.body:
St Clair defines mahogany as a red brown, after the hardwood [1]. Our library lists this darker swatch in three systems: RAL 8016, a paint standard whose screen value is approximate, ISCC-NBS block 43, and Maerz and Paul's dictionary, which records the name as early as 1892 [2]. A near-twin there is called Red Currant, dated 1899 [2]. Its lighter, redder sister is [[mahogany-red]], and the plain color is [[mahogany]].

Brown can also be an end point. Daniel Thompson, a translator of Cennino, noted that the river landscapes of Baldovinetti and Domenico Veneziano must once have had green verdigris, which has since gone mahogany brown [3]. Some of the browns in old paintings were not painted brown.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Dark red-browns are common in the museum record. In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 3,852 (16.2 per cent) hold a color within six units over at least five per cent of the canvas, peaking in the 1500s at 560 of 2,231 works [4]. Darkened varnish and dark grounds probably push those numbers up, and the archive cannot separate them from the painter's original color [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [4]. Compare [[brown]].
